newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish construction starts rise 8 pct in March-May.
newsitem.headline: Danish construction starts rise 8 pct in March-May.

text.p: Danish construction starts rose a seasonally adjusted eight percent in March to May 1997 compared with the December-February quarter, but were three percent below March-May 1996, the National Statistics Office said on Wednesday.
It said activity hads been exceptionally low in the previous quarter, and fell sharply in May from an unusually high level in April.
The figures are based on the ground area under construction, and refer to all construction projects, public and private.

Mortgage-lender Nykredit's banking subsidiary, Nykredit Bank, said the figures indicated that construction growth had reached its maximum, reducing the danger of wage inflation in the construction industry.
"It is for the time being our evaluation that new building has peaked. This is due to the government's freeze on public construction," the bank wrote in a commentary on Wednesday's figures.

It said that it expected a fall in employment in the civil engineering industry in 1997 and 1998 because of the completion last spring of the Great Belt bridge and tunnel link between the Danish mainland and the island of Fyn and the end of the land-based phase of another link between Copenhagen and the southern Swedish city of Malmo.
But it said it was still too early to revise its forecasts of average 2.1 percent inflation in 1997 and 2.5 percent in 1998. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969653
